Importer ordering and EH visibility have focused IR coverage, not runtime EH parity. SIMD normalization preserves its output base type in controlled EE metadata cases, not generated SIMD execution.
Generic virtual lookup handle kinds and array dimension local reuse have controlled EE/IR coverage, not NativeAOT-generated call or multidimensional-array execution parity.
Shared instantiation construction preserves direct/indirect method/class handles and readonly-array behavior in controlled EE cases. Its Wasm ldvirtftn integration remains unvalidated on that target.

Owned and inherited async context chains preserve argument order and frame metadata in focused IR cases. Cached EE async metadata is checked across repeated and per-compiler queries, including GC during the pinned call. SaveAsyncContexts has root-method coverage for capture/fault/return ordering, context arguments, OSR, initialization, existing EH regions, non-returning bodies, and void/scalar/return-buffer-address merging. Inline phase execution, multi-register struct returns, and async lowering remain unverified; fgVerifyHandlerTab is still an existing diagnostic stub.

Async-version void/scalar return wrapping, hidden arguments, default ValueTask folding, static monitor lookup and ReadyToRun entrypoints have controlled IR/EE coverage. Struct/constructor folding, inline return wrapping and synchronized async-return execution remain unexercised; this does not establish async codegen parity.

Async-version tail patterns, EE tailcall consent, async metadata, protected-region recognition, and own-versus-inherited inline contexts have focused coverage. SaveAsyncContexts now produces the generated EH IDs and saved-context arguments. Prefix integration, covariant return cleanup, and runtime tail-await execution remain unexercised by the corpus.
Conditional Wasm address-mode recognition passed isolated managed probes; declaration and ARM64 threshold synchronization does not establish non-x64 target support.
The managed calli corpus case reaches imported CALL ind IR; it does not establish unmanaged calli conversion, NativeAOT fat-pointer execution, or codegen parity.
Instrumented value-profile collection and constrained boxing order are source-reconciled but remain unexercised by the current corpus.

The importer/intrinsic batches pass localized managed checks and a subsequent NativeAOT/native-host corpus capture. That corpus does not exercise Half expansion, helper-to-user conversion, generic Memmove, multidimensional stores, span spilling, runtime async expansions or non-x64 paths; no execution/codegen evidence is claimed for them. The new custom-awaiter-in-continuation optimization and its main-call hook remain unported; continuation-member descriptors and registration now exist, but layout and lowering remain unported.

Inline placeholder and candidate-diagnostic support has focused coverage for effects, node identity, nested substitution, block flags, byref retyping, constant branches and prior failures. Windows-x64 expression folding is active; successful EE-backed late devirtualization, multi-register struct repair and full inlining are not established.

Inline argument/prelude/epilogue integration has focused coverage for live-edge substitution, pseudo-argument classification, struct-load faults, initialization, GC-local cleanup and null-check ordering. EE-backed cctor insertion and full inline-phase execution remain unexercised.

Recursive-inline guards preserve exact-context rejection, depth-observation ordering, the implementation depth bound, and the 64-type generic-loading threshold in controlled EE tests. Implicit-byref demotion cleanup covers retained/undone/no promotion; global morph and end-to-end generic inlining remain unverified.

Async inline-frame return helpers preserve cold resumption branches, caller context loads, frame-depth slot sharing, resumed-indicator propagation through retained fault handlers, and symbolic-offset cloning/dumps in focused IR/EE cases, including invocation through inline block splicing. Successful helper inlining, continuation layout and async lowering remain unverified.

Inline invocation rollback and failed-call cleanup have controlled EE coverage. Managed exception trapping and synthetic native SEH unwinding pass a Windows-x64 NativeAOT probe, but real EE-thrown failures and successful nested inline compilation remain unexercised. Expression folding is complete on Windows x64; fgInline stays disabled pending its remaining phase-closure audit.

Tree-form scalar folding preserves logical IDs and has exact native import-prefix coverage for six folds. Replacement requires unthreaded source nodes; value numbering, cached post-morph argument aliases and LIR replacement remain unsupported. The full inliner remains disabled.

Floating constant-operand folding preserves native signed-zero and NaN rules, full-optimization gates, effects and JTRUE relop roots. Its four identity folds have exact import-prefix coverage; NaN/effect combinations have focused IR coverage, not codegen evidence. VN support and global-morph assertion closure remain incomplete.

Integral ranges and tree-based non-negativity have focused cast/IR coverage and retain the existing corpus prefixes. VN-dependent non-negativity fails explicitly when tree facts are insufficient. Assertion generation, global morph, non-x64 execution and range-driven codegen are not established.

Non-HWI folding covers integer identities, identical comparisons, conditional selection and nullable-box comparisons. FoldInteger has an exact import prefix for its mask-to-cast fold; Roslyn removes multiply-by-zero, while existing importer handling removes divide-by-one before this folding helper. Those identities, effect gates and conditional/nullable cases also have focused IR coverage. Full inline/global-morph activation remains pending.

The Windows-x64 HWI dispatcher has focused IR coverage, including conversion cancellation, mask rewrites, scalar upper lanes, uniform/per-lane shifts, bounds, comparison normalization, side effects and VN refresh. The eleven-method NativeAOT capture retains the six existing exact import prefixes; FoldHardware diverges because impHWIntrinsic still returns no imported intrinsic. Non-xarch folding and vector execution parity are not established.
The eleven-method corpus contains no EH or pinned-local cases and establishes neither full-phase nor codegen parity.
